title: Plant Reproduction
standard_text: Flowering plants reproduce sexually through flowers: pollination, fertilization, and seed and fruit formation; seeds are dispersed and germinate. Some plants reproduce asexually from stems, roots or leaves. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 2: Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Living Things): parts of a flower, pollination, seed dispersal, germination and asexual reproduction. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Some plants grow from stems, roots or leaves.
body_html:
How to think about it

The flower is the reproductive part of a plant. The stamen (anther and filament) makes pollen; the pistil (stigma, style and ovary) holds the ovules. Pollination moves pollen to the stigma by wind, insects or birds. After fertilization the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.

Some plants reproduce without seeds (asexual reproduction): new sweet potato plants grow from roots, sugarcane from stem cuttings, kalanchoe from leaves, and bananas from suckers. The young plants are like the parent.

Example

Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?

It holds the ovules.

Answer: the ovary

Example

How does a banana plant make new plants?

From the base of the plant

Answer: from suckers (asexual)

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up pollination and fertilization.
  • Thinking only animals reproduce.
  • Thinking all plants need seeds to reproduce.

items.q: Is the stigma part of the male or the female part of a flower?
items.e: The stamen (anther and filament) is male; the pistil (stigma, style and ovary) is female.

items.q: “The ovule grows into a seed, and the ovary becomes a fruit.” What happened just before?
c: A bee visits a flower and pollen sticks to its body.
The bee carries the pollen to another flower of the same kind.
The pollen joins with an ovule in the ovary (fertilization).
The seeds are dispersed and can grow into new plants.
items.e: Pollination → fertilization → seed and fruit → dispersal.

items.q: Does a seed need light to germinate?
c: No. A seed can germinate without it.

items.e: Seeds can germinate on wet cotton balls in the dark. They need light later, when the young plant grows.
